summary: This tutorial explains how to perform peer review in LibreOffice Writer using document versioning. You start by opening an existing document and enabling "Record Changes" under the "Edit" menu. This allows you to track specific edits made by different users. For example, you can insert comments, delete text, or make other modifications. Each change is timestamped and attributed to the user who made it. To revert changes, you can simply delete the marked lines. The document displays edited text in a different color, making it easy to distinguish between original and modified content. When you open a document reviewed by others, you see the edits and deletions made by reviewers. The tutorial demonstrates this process using documents like "sevenreasonstoadoptfoss.odt" and "governmentsupportforfossinindia.odt," showing how multiple edits and deletions have been tracked and displayed.
